ip_top_stories.title: Sony Copyright Suit Survives AI Music Generator's Dismissal Bid
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has allowed Sony's copyright infringement lawsuit against an AI music generator to proceed, rejecting the defendant's motion to dismiss. The case is an important development in music industry litigation against AI companies over unauthorised use of copyrighted material. Multiple outlets covered the ruling, confirming its significance to the broader AI copyright landscape.

ip_top_stories.title: Copyright owners v AI developers: the emerging trends
ip_top_stories.summary: An analysis of the evolving legal landscape between copyright owners and AI developers, mapping the key trends emerging from litigation, licensing negotiations, and policy debates. The piece examines how rights holders are asserting claims and how AI companies are responding.

ip_top_stories.title: EU copyright law roundup – first trimester of 2026
ip_top_stories.summary: A comprehensive roundup of European Union copyright law developments in the first trimester of 2026, covering legislative updates, case law, and regulatory activity relevant to AI and digital content. The piece provides an authoritative overview of the EU's evolving copyright framework as it applies to AI training and use.

ip_top_stories.title: Monkey selfie from 15 years ago accidentally sets precedent for AI copyright dispute
ip_top_stories.summary: The landmark 'monkey selfie' case, which established that non-human authors cannot hold copyright, is now being cited as an inadvertent precedent in disputes over AI-generated content. Legal commentators note the ruling's relevance to questions of authorship and ownership when AI systems produce creative works.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Makes Securing Copyright Protection for Software Code Tricky Guide
ip_top_stories.summary: An examination of the challenges AI-assisted code generation creates for software copyright protection, covering how courts and practitioners are grappling with questions of authorship, originality, and ownership when AI tools contribute substantially to code. The piece outlines practical and legal considerations for developers and rights holders.

ip_further_links.title: Is the government's stance on AI copyright holding back the UK tech scene?
ip_further_links.summary: An assessment of whether the UK government's current position on AI and copyright law is hindering domestic AI development and investment.

ip_further_links.title: AI Startups Have These Copyright Lawyers on Speed Dial
ip_further_links.summary: A look at the specialist copyright lawyers advising AI startups as IP disputes multiply across the industry.

ip_further_links.title: Anthropic Code Crisis Creates Copyright Contradiction
ip_further_links.summary: Reports of an internal Anthropic coding incident have raised questions about the company's own position on copyright when its AI systems reproduce or closely replicate existing code.

ip_further_links.title: Who owns AI copyright when machines create art?
ip_further_links.summary: An overview of the unresolved legal question of ownership when AI systems independently generate creative works, surveying current positions in different jurisdictions.

ip_further_links.title: AI-generated content should be clearly labelled to help people spot fakes, committee says — The Globe and Mail
ip_further_links.summary: A parliamentary or regulatory committee has recommended mandatory labelling of AI-generated content as a measure to help audiences distinguish it from human-created work.

ip_further_links.title: Analysing China's stricter examination standards for AI-related patent applications
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of China's tightened patent examination standards for AI-related inventions and what this means for applicants seeking protection in that jurisdiction.

ip_further_links.title: Bologna Children's Book Fair 2026: AI Takes Center Stage [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: AI's role in children's publishing was a dominant theme at the 2026 Bologna Children's Book Fair, with discussions covering both the opportunities and IP concerns raised by AI-generated illustrations and content.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — Exploring Data Spaces in Scholarly Communications
ip_further_links.summary: An exploration of how 'data spaces' — shared, governed data infrastructures — could reshape data sharing and licensing in scholarly communications.

ip_further_links.title: AI in the patent industry: Don't believe the hype. Believe the data.
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat examines empirical data on AI adoption in the patent industry, questioning inflated claims about AI's transformative impact on patent prosecution and examination.

ip_further_links.title: GitHub Policy Update
ip_further_links.summary: GitHub has updated its policies in ways that have implications for AI-generated code, copyright ownership, and developer rights on the platform.
